anomalies.observed: Both GND1 and GND2 pins of the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 are connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: For galvanic isolation, GND1 (logic side) and GND2 (bus side) should be on separate ground nets (e.g., GND and GND_ISO).

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) ... U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in)

anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier is bypassed, so the CAN buses are not galvanically isolated, defeating the purpose of the isolated transceivers and potentially causing ground loops or damage.

anomalies.observed: R60 is connected between D30.2 (cathode of the e-stop indicator LED) and ESTOP_OUT, while D30.4 (anode) is also on ESTOP_OUT. This creates a closed loop with no path to ground.
anomalies.expected: R60 should be connected between D30.2 and GND to limit LED current and allow the LED to indicate ESTOP_OUT state.
anomalies.impact: The e-stop indicator LED (D30 second element) will never light because both ends of the series LED-resistor path are on the same net, so no current can flow.

anomalies.observed: The VP (positive supply) pins of the ESD protection arrays U4 and U23 are left unconnected.
anomalies.expected: VP should be connected to the appropriate supply rail (e.g., +3V3 or +5V) to provide complete ESD clamping for the Ethernet data lines.
anomalies.impact: Positive ESD transients on the Ethernet lines are not clamped to a supply rail, reducing the effectiveness of the ESD protection.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple anomalies: the isolated CAN transceivers have their logic and bus grounds tied together, defeating isolation; the e-stop indicator LED resistor R60 is miswired to ESTOP_OUT instead of GND, so the LED never lights; and the ESD protection arrays U4/U23 have their VP pins left unconnected.
